Penn Cole, Bianca Paulevici (Translator)

4.17

Volumul 1 din Saga Blestemul Seminției

Într-o lume a muritorilor colonizată de zei și condusă de Descendenți, nemiloșii lor urmași, Diem Bellator tânjește să scape de viața izolată din satul ei sărac.

Iar dispariția bruscă a mamei sale și descoperirea unui secret periculos despre trecutul ei îi oferă lui Diem ocazia neașteptată de a pătrunde în lumea întunecată a regalității Descendenților și de a dezlega încrengătura de mistere lăsate în urmă de mama ei.

Dar cu moștenitorul regelui muribund ‒ un Descendent chipeș și misterios ‒ care îi urmărește fiecare mișcare din Palatul Regal și cu o înverșunată alianță a muritorilor care o recrutează pentru a se alătura războiului civil gata să izbucnească, Diem va trebui să navigheze printre regulile nescrise ale dragostei, ale puterii și ale politicii pentru a-și salva familia și întreaga omenire muritoare.

About the author

Penn Cole

13 books12.3k followers
While my life has taken me through a lot of ups and downs, my love for reading and writing has forever been my true north. I’ve been writing stories since my childhood, filling mountains of notebooks with wild worlds and angsty romances. After a detour as an attorney and small business owner, I am thrilled to finally be pursuing my lifelong dream of becoming an author.

Though I’m a Texas girl born and bred, I currently live in France with my husband, where I can usually be found drinking far too much wine and eating far, far too many pastries.

SK

August 24, 2023
"I'm not afraid, Devourer of Crowns, Ravager of Realms, Herald of Vengeance."

✔️ Enemies to lovers
✔️ Slow burn
✔️ Fiesty fmc x brooding prince
✔️ "Touch her and die"

Huh, am kinda conflicted about this one. There were some good bits but the second half in particular was quite messy.

Starting with the world building is simplistic and fairly easy to understand. Although, I would have loved for the author to build more on it as it does seem interesting but I don't have much to picture it. The pacing of the book is quite fast and is consistent.

The first half is really well written. I enjoyed it as the characters were introduced and the stage was being set. But as I closed in towards the second half, I realized not much has happened, at least nothing significant. This is where the author messed up. So not only she attempts to speed things up plot wise, she has realised that the romance was not set up properly and in order to achieve that, she misses out on angst, feelings, emotions for a slow burn. The author also makes the "badass fmc" turn into a really "dumbass fmc" and it was something that really annoyed me.

Diem, our fmc is truly fiesty. I really liked her in the first half. Her personality was so balanced and she seemed mature. Her powers were something that intrigued me throughout the book, so no complaints there. But the problem started in the second half when she continues to despise the mmc, Luther, for no strongly backed reason. She also loses her personality when she joins the Guardians. Spy work did not suit her at all. She continues to make poor decisions even though she is presented as a smart woman in the first half. By talking down to the 'soon to be king' in front of his subjects just for the sake of being fiesty did not suit her. Her mood swings gave me whiplash. Her powers deserved more clarity.

Luther, the dark brooding prince with a scar on his face sounds hot. But I have no opinion of him. He doesn't have enough screen time. He was there for about 30% of the book? He went from staring at her, occasionally having some conversations to "touch her and die" which did not suit him. The trope came across as included just for the sake of it. His protectiveness for her did not make sense at all when nothing happened.

The supporting characters- I didn't like Henri from the start. It seems he's going to become a Tamlin like personality soon, I hope to be proven wrong. I like Teller, who was Diem's brother. I honestly couldn't careless about their mother or father. Maura was a good friend but Diem did her dirty.

The romance is presented as slow burn enemies to lovers, both fall short. The slow burned did not burn at all, and there was no angst. It shouldn't be called enemies to lovers. It was more of "I'm a fiesty girl so am supposed to despise him but there's no genuine reason for it." I don't believe that Luther ever despised her, he just never knew her enough. The emotions and romance hit all of a sudden around 80-85% mark and it felt out of place. There was little chemistry. Hopefully, the second book will be better in that regard.

The ending was okayish. The epilogue was super confusing. Again, I do not care about the mother. Never really see her enough to care.

Tbh it has a lot of potential but the second half was a mess. The author rushed it all, and it directly makes it look like a poorly executed book. It could have used a few more 100-200 pages and then the romance and character building would've been immaculate.
I'm still gonna read the second book and see what happens but fingers crossed🤞

~•~•~
Been hearing a lot of positive things about this one. Let's see how it goes🤞

My Honest Book Review: [Spark of the Everflame by Penn Cole]

Check out my other book reviews in this series!
[Glow of the Everflame by Penn Cole]
[Heat of the Everflame by Penn Cole]

This book reminded me of my first love, Red Queen by Victoria Aveyard. So if you like that series, you will certainly love the vibes of this one.

Spark of the Everflame is a spellbinding journey into a world where ancient secrets and powerful destinies collide. From the moment I delved into the pages of this captivating fantasy romance, I was enraptured by its intricate plot, rich world-building, and compelling characters.

The story follows Diem Bellator, a young woman yearning for answers about her missing mother and as she was searching, she was discovering some truths about herself. As old secrets unravel and newfound powers emerge, Diem finds herself thrust into a world of Descended royalty, political intrigue, and forbidden love. Diem's journey is not just about unraveling the mysteries of her past but also finding her place in a world torn apart by war and ambition.

Penn Cole's writing is nothing short of enchanting, weaving a tapestry of magic, and complex relationships that kept me turning pages late into the night. The slow burn romance between Diem and the heir to the throne adds a layer of tension and longing that will resonate with fans of epic fantasy and enemies-to-lovers tropes.

If you're a fan of immersive fantasy worlds, strong heroines, and epic romance, "Spark of the Everflame" is a must-read that will leave you eagerly anticipating the next installment in this captivating saga. Penn Cole has crafted a gem of a novel that sparks the imagination and kindles the flames of excitement for what's to come. Highly recommended for lovers of magic, dragons, and epic adventures!

Okay we flew through this book....it made me want to write a review after a very long time so five stars for that alone 😭

The writing was very consistent. I would say personally for me, the beginning was a bit slow but it picked up in the middle and the final 10-12 chapters had me sitting at the same spot flying through this book. It was very easy to read and understand, and I, who has not read fantasy in like a long time thought it was easy to dive into this world- whereas it usually harder to grasp things when you start a fantasy novel.

The characters, Diem, I loved her so much!! She had that perfect amount of rage and I love reading heated scenes, they are perfectly overwhelming 😭 I like that raging was not her only personality, she was stubborn when there was need of it, and she showed vulnerability at times as well, there was this mysterious aura affiliated with her character that also intrigued me. Luthor, I love it when we don't get a lot of the main love interest in a massive series. I love how Luthor was introduced to us at the near start and then again near the end of the second half. His character was set up perfectly and made me love him even more. He was broody but not without reason, and I liked that. Henri, nahhh fuck off.

Romance, it wasn't the main focus, and I didnt mind it. The few glimpses that we saw were enough to promise us more of it with better development. Plot, I really liked!! the plot twist, I kinda knew but it still had me like whaaaa. The end did catch me off guard because like woah I ddint expect that. From about 30% forward I started disliking this book more and more.

Edit to change rating from 2 Stars to 3 Stars

The story is set in a mortal world colonized by gods and ruled over by descended.

Diem is our FMC and is a trainee/assistant healer to her mother who is the chief healer for the kingdom- mortal and descended. One day after eavesdropping on a questionable mysterious conversation that her mother is having with one of the descended and after her own run in with a shady woman with magical powers who knows everything about Diem (things no one else knows) her mother disappears. This opens the opportunity for Diem to become chief healer and basically be the doctor on call for the descended and giving her access to the palace. When she shows up to an emergency call at the palace one day, she heals the princess - it seems as though she did it with some kind of magic but brushes it off saying it was the princess’s healing properties (even though for her age she doesn’t have powerful enough healing abilities to heal from a lethal wound) okay, now I’m interested right?

All of the descendants have light eyes, all mortals have brown. Diem was born with auburn hair and brown eyes, but at a young age that faded away and she now has white hair and grey eyes which is questionable- is she a descendant? Is she a half mortal half descendant?

Lemme go back to that shady woman conversation- basically Diem has been taking this powder for almost her whole life, when she first lost her hair color and eye color she had what she described to be hallucinations and with this powder she took it made them go away- the shady witch like woman told her to stop taking it, and of course she does.

From this point forward I really start to get frustrated and annoyed. Without the powder there’s this inner voice that keeps yelling at Diem to fight, and destroy. Not just the mortals and not just the descendants- literally anyone that she disagrees with- like to the point she wants to shred them apart and literally destroy them. Friends and family 🤷🏻‍♀️ doesn’t matter.

As the story moves along, I find Diem to be so erratic, irrational, and hypocritical.
She decides to be a spy for the “guardians” (a group working against the royals) yet she’s the total opposite of a spy. Drawing every attention in the world to her and not being remotely stealthy. She flip flops on her loyalty all the while this inner voice keeps yelling at her to fight and destroy literally everyone that NGL it gave me mf anxiety! Like she was possessed or something.

These descendants are portrayed to be so evil and so powerful that they can wipe out a mortals life with the snap of a finger and yet Diem is blatantly defiant and crossing the line with no strategy, knowledge or regard for her life or her brothers life that is tied up in this agreement to be the doctor on call for the royals. Is she a feisty, stabby FMC? Sure, but without any concern for herself or her family. Look, I get plot armor but this was too much for me to believe.

With the king deathly ill the crown is to be passed down to the next most powerful descendant. It’s not a choice of the kingdom but is passed on by magic- we think we know who that’s going to be but do we really?

This book is getting high praise but the pacing was off for me in the middle of the book and all this back and forth with the FMC as far as loyalty really just bothered me. I get she’s young and is learning etc but she makes all these big bold moves based on nothing more than a pissed off teenager in my opinion. I found myself not really liking her or almost anyone around mid story. I do really like Lily the Princess, the FMC brother Teller and the mysterious Prince Luther.

I feel like there’s a lot to work with here, it didn’t really come together for me personally, I found the FMC to be really grating and not fleshed out very well, I may read book 2 which is out this week just to see if that happens..

I’m conflicted. And I mostly have myself to blame for going into this book with extremely high expectations… nonetheless there were definitely some good bits and pieces, but the story as a whole didn’t really suck me in until the 75% mark.

The world building was easy to follow but i found it to be lacking a bit simply because I wanted MORE! The world itself was very intriguing but I feel like I only got bits and pieces of it.

My biggest issue with this book is that it felt extremely slow. Not much at all happened in the first half and I found myself very bored and underwhelmed. The romance was set up so late in that it felt really rushed and unbelievable. The author spent so much time introducing Diem however managed to not give us enough to really understand her actions in the second half…

Speaking of our FMC Diem: she’s definitely fiesty and I found her to be intriguing in the beginning with a lot of potential! But towards the middle of the book she started to make incredibly stupid decisions that didn’t really fit her character we were initially introduced to. And her constant show of misplaced hatred towards Luther started to get on my nerves because of how obvious it was that she had no reason to hate him. Her mood was all over the place but I think that was for a reason… I honestly didn’t find her character annoying though, it was obvious she was sheltered her whole life and so beyond naive to the world around her, she seems to be the type of character that has a LOT of work to do and will only frustrate me more before I grow to love her and… I can handle that.

Luther our MMC carried and he was barely in this book. He maybe made an appearance for all of 20% of the story. Which I think was an incredibly missed opportunity, but I have a feeling book 2 will make up for it! I mean he’s a dark, broody, clearly traumatized shadow daddy so of course I’m going to fall in love with him…. But at the moment I don’t have enough of his character to really form an opinion! It was odd that after spending little to no time with Diem he whipped out “touch her and die” energy, his feels seemed so abrupt and out of nowhere. But clearly there’s a reason for that.. I hope.

This romance in this book is advertised as a slow burn enemies to lovers but I really wouldn’t call it that at all (at least not yet). Because we didn’t get much Luther until the end, there was no time for their romance to even begin burning… no tension, no angst, but oh there is so much potential for it! Also the “enemies” aspect was essentially non existent. Diem was just too sheltered and guarded to see past her misplaced anger and ended up projecting it on to Luther, it was clear he never hated her. However how they ended really gave me hope…. I feel a SCRUMPTIOUS slow burn brewing!!

The side characters weren’t anything special to me yet. Henri gave me the ick on multiple occasions and is entirely Tamlin and Matt Donovan coded, iykyk.

The last 20% really redeemed this book for me and set up book 2 really well! Hopefully that set the stage for how things will progress in this series!

I was definitely expecting more and was underwhelmed by this book but it did show enough potential for me to be excited to jump in to book 2! Hopefully it’s only up from here…

“Don’t choose a mediocre life for a mediocre man. Go be exceptional.”

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ✦ . 　⁺ 　 . ━ 2.8-3.0 ☆ ━ . 　⁺ 　 . ✦
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ╰┈➤˗ˏˋㅤmight contain spoilers ❗

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I genuinely don't even want to write this review, but I am doing it only because I want to be able to jump right into the second book with the hope that you all did not lie to me and it will indeed be better that whatever this one was supposed to be. And I also do not really wish to write this review because I am not sure what I am supposed to say in regards to a 300-page introduction for an 80-page-long book; that is exactly how I felt reading this novel. Therefore, I will try my best to keep this review as short as possible and I do apologies if it will not be as extensive as usual, but I am truthfully unsure what I could say.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ "Spark of the Everflame" transports you in the realm of Lumnos, where you are following the story of Diem Bellator, a fearless mortal healer who is somehow constantly drawn to danger at all times following the sudden disappearance of her mother. Oh, and I forgot to mention that she is not like other girls, she is different. Being left with only her father and brother, Diem struggles to keep her life normal while the enigma of her mother's disappearance keeps pushing her to seek answers. Despite the clear warning of her family to stay away from the powerful Descended and their magic and especially from the palace and the royal family, Diem finds herself drawn towards the people responsible for the poor life condition of the mortals and especially towards the very brooding, dark and of course, absolutely gorgeous Prince of Lumnos, Luther. Since apparently she cannot keep her mouth shut or do the right thing for the love of all that is good in the world, Diem (the girl who is NOT like other girls) soon turns from a very fiery, yet kind healer, to a pawn caught in the middle of the political intrigues between the Descended and The Guardians, these creepy Power Rangers of the realms who are fighting to offer a better life for the mortals.
ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ Therefore a simple, loving life together with her childhood, boring and annoying best friend might not seem just as beautiful and satisfying to Diem anymore, and the secrets that were kept from her might have consequences she could not even dream of. Revenge, hate, and love all stem from passion, and one small misstep could have burning repercussions.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I somehow feel like I presented the summary of this book way more fast-paced and intriguing than it actually is, but I suppose I will just expand more on it below.


ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ -ˋˏ ༻ world-building, writing and action ༺ ˎˊ-

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I genuinely enjoy the way the world-building was used and presented in this novel. I am aware this is going to be a series of books, so I absolutely adore it when the first book in the series brings only the suitable amount of world-building elements and information, which are required to better understand the events of the book. I am convinced the further you go into the series, more details will come to light, but for now I am absolutely content with what was revealed up until now. I do hope the rest of the series will not disappoint.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍As it seems to be a trend lately for the books I am reading, there isn't much I have to say in terms of the writing. It is just, once again, a very easy-to-read book with a quite suitable register and normal writing that anyone would find entertaining. I would, however, advise you to watch out for some really big grammar errors which I hope will be fixed once the book is officially released.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I admit, I was kind of disappointed about the action of the book itself. This is not an extremely short book, therefore, when I am looking at all the events that actually happened in this book, I cannot consider myself satisfied with the pace and the plot itself. The book felt somehow latent and even a bit repetitive at times. Apart from the very last 15% of the book, I felt like I was only reading about Diem's bad choices and brainless decisions over and over again in a terrifyingly annoying loop. I do hope the second book picks-up the pace and brings way more of the plot into play.


ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ -ˋˏ ༻ characters ༺ ˎˊ-

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ I am not sure if it is me growing old, or if it is the characters themselves that are acting way too childish, because I just finished this book and I swear on whatever you want me to that I DID NOT care a single moment about any of these characters; which honestly disappointed me because I really wanted to get attached to them.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ❇ Diem (she is not like other girls) - I promised myself I will try to stop being a hater in my reviews, but this girl is just testing my patience. if "i cannot make a good decision for the love of all that is holy" and "if being dumb would be illegal, this book would have never been published" were given a written form, it would be this character. I have never wanted to have the possibility of smacking a character more than now in my entire life. This girl is simply unable to make one right decision, and she is simply, absolutely oblivious to everything that happens RIGHT BEFORE HER EYES; she also has absolutely no sense of respect and self-preservation, and her naivety reaches heights that I am pretty sure should be considered impossible. Please, please tell me she starts getting better soon, otherwise I might literally have a mental breakdown.

ㅤ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ‍‍‍‍‍‍ ❇ Luther - I am pretty sure I would have loved him if we got more of his character in this book. But I am patient, I am waiting; I am seeing all that potential hidden under this cliché dark, brooding man with a heart of gold. I just really hope he will not be made into the man who suddenly loses all his brain functional areas and his basic mental abilities in front of the woman he loves.

For anyone who has every been told their spark shouldn't burn so bright
and for all the people who loved them precisely because it did.

THE PLOT

Diem Bellator yearns to escape her mortal world that has been colonized by the gods and ruled over my the Descended, their offspring. After her mother's disappearance (and a dangerous, secret discovery about her past), Diem is offered the opportunity to enter the dark work of Descended royalty and uncover the truth behind her mothers disappearance. Now that the King is dying, Luther, his son, is watching her every move, and Diem must unravel the world of magic, politics, and love before war ensues.

MY THOUGHTS

The Plot: I absolutely DEVOURED this book and its plot. The entire thing was just written to perfection. I loved the politics and the world building. There was always something going on but it never felt crowded enough to the point where it got jumbled! There were twists and turns and everything in between and I just ate it up. Ate it all up. The politics played a major part in this book, as well as the magic system. I think it was written and explained so well!! The only thing I'd say would be that sometimes it got confusing with the amount of subplots and trying to keep up with them. This book has left me speechless. The ending of this book??? MY JAW WAS ON THE DAMN FLOOR. I was NOT expecting the ending and I just know I'm going to love the rest of this series. This first book set up such a good standard for the rest of the series that I hope keeps up!!

The Characters: Diem was one of the strongest FMC's I've read this year. I loved her. So. Much!!! SO MUCH!! She was so witty and sarcastic and has such a badass attitude. It's Diem's world and we're all just living in it. I really do not like Henri. I could not get into his affection and love for Diem from the very beginning I don't know why I just couldn't. As the book went on, my feelings were justified. Henri can kiss my ass. Now let's talk about Luther. Luther and Diem? I am ROOTING. If they don't end up together I'm gonna riot I loved them so much. Their personalities just fit so well together and the chemistry??? Off the charts. I was eating up their tension with a knife and a fork.

Overall, I can already tell this series is going to have a special place in my heart. I'm a little intimidated by the amount of pages in the next books but at this point I don't even care I will eat up every last bit of it. This is an adult slow-burn romantasy that I recommend everyone give a try at some point!!! Loved Loved Loved. 🩷

FAVORITE SCENES AND QUOTES

"That's what family is all about. Standing by each others side, even when you make the worst mistakes."

But I was made of swinging fists and rash words, my edges too jagged and my temper too hot. Nothing about me was delicate.

I knew I should be more worried, perhaps try to convince him away from an activity that could so easily get him killed, but it kindled a hearth in my heart to see him full of joy again. Maybe he needed a purpose as much as I did.

"Don't choose a mediocre life for a mediocre man. Go be exceptional. If he's worth it, he won't judge you. And if he's really the one, he'll come along for the ride."

"You're mortal, remember? Your body is too fragile."
"First of all, if you ever call me fragile again, I'll slice your precious royal balls off and shove them down your throat."

"You think I fear my own death? Every day I draw breath is as much a curse as a gift. I've been living on borrowed time for longer than you can imagine. If you're the way my fate finally catches up to me, I can't fathom a more beautiful end."

“You think I fear my own death?” he whispered in my ear. “Every day I draw breath is as much a curse as a gift. I’ve been living on borrowed time for longer than you can imagine. If you’re the way my fate finally catches up to me, I can’t fathom a more beautiful end.”

I’ve been loving diving into more fantasy lately, and Spark of the Everflame was such a fun surprise. It’s one of those books that completely pulls you into its world, it’s full of divine rulers, rebellious mortals, and a heroine who’s way tougher (and more stubborn) than anyone gives her credit for.

The story follows Diem, a village girl whose life takes a wild turn when her mother goes missing and some long buried secrets about her own past start to surface. Suddenly she’s tangled up in royal politics, ancient powers, and a rebellion that might change everything. It’s got all the juicy fantasy elements, prophecies, magic, betrayal, plus a slow burn romance that had me grinning and groaning in equal measure.

Penn Cole’s writing flows so easily that before I knew it, I’d flown through half the book. I loved how she built a world that feels both rich and lived in without dumping a ton of info on you. And Diem? She’s such a great mix of vulnerable and fierce, the kind of character you just want to cheer for.

If you like your fantasy with a side of tension filled banter, emotional twists, and that addictive “just one more chapter” feeling, this one’s a great pick. I can totally see why everyone’s been talking about it and honestly, I can’t wait to see where the next book goes.

I Highly Recommend.

What to Expect:

➼ First Person Single POV

Am I bumping this to five stars because of Luther? Maybe… but it was at least a high four for me without him factored in. 😆 Lord, he is a grade A book boyfriend though. 🥰

This was a highly anticipated read for me, but I had heard enough negative opinions about Diem going into this that I wasn’t sure how I’d feel about her. My opinion of her could definitely go down in the next book, but so far I’m really not understanding what it is about her that people don’t like. I was frankly pretty impressed by how she handled herself. She made some mistakes along the way, but she continually weighed her actions against her personal understanding of right and wrong and changed her opinion and corrected her path when she realized she was at fault. Both sides had compelling arguments and I could see how anyone would struggle with some of the decisions she had to make. So much of her history had been hidden from her and it would make sense for her to struggle with those revelations.

The ending wasn’t completely unexpected, but I was a little surprised by the timing. I expected that to happen a little further down the line… This was a solid start to the series and I’m anxious to start book two! Hopefully she doesn’t become as annoying as people say… 😅

₊· ͟͟͞͞➳ Review may contain minor spoilers and quotes

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Overview: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

⁀જ➣꒰ ⋮ ρℓσт.꒱

For being the first book in a romantasy series, this kept me very entertained. I really enjoyed the worldbuilding in this book. The plotline itself isn’t unique—corrupt kingdom, rebels, wars, all the things you’d find in every romantasy. But the magic system was very interesting. The politics of this world and the history were fascinating.

There are obviously some answers we need to unravel, but it's not a 4-book series for nothing. I was able to guess the plot twists in this book. One was very obvious to me, so it didn’t shock me when it was revealed, and one was a surprise because I didn’t think it could actually happen.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ 𝕽𝖔𝖒𝖆𝖓𝖈𝖊.꒱

I hated the “romance” between her and Henri. It was just…there. It didn’t feel necessary to me, and I kept hoping it would end soon.

The issue I have with the “enemies-to-lovers” trope is that it is never done right. In certain books, it just feels like a marketing ploy to get readers to read their books. While Diem and Luther certainly hated each other, I wouldn’t put their relationship under this trope. Diem's feelings for Luther felt forced, because she hated him for...no reason. The book made it seem like Luther hated her, but I never felt that he did.

Also, having heard this series was the slowest of slow burns, I expected them to kiss around the end of book two. They kiss at the end of this book, which, hey, I’m not complaining—but I wouldn’t say this is a slow burn; maybe my mind will change in the next book? I loved the tension between her and Luther, but I wouldn’t say it’s the best I’ve ever read.

⁀જ➣꒰⋮ ᭙𝕣ⅈ𝕥ⅈꪀᧁ.꒱

The writing was very simple and easy to understand. The plotline is easy to follow, so you won’t feel like your mind will explode from the several questions you get in more complex magic systems. I appreciate the fact that the author didn't info-dump on the readers.

══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══╡ Characters: ╞══⋆⋅☆⋅⋆══

જ⁀➴ Diem: I don’t love her or hate her, but she can be very…stupid. She very clearly lacks critical thinking. Her feelings on pretty much everything around her felt all over the place. Her “rage” was so bland to me, as well. Her decisions are very irrational, and that makes her a terrible spy. There was this one scene where she did something VERY dumb, and I kept thinking to myself, there is no way she didn’t come up with a plan and think of the consequences before executing it. That scene pissed me off. There were other times when I understood her actions, but the consequences of those actions irritated the hell out of me. Sometimes she gave me a “not like the other girls” vibe, and that gave me the ick, too. That being said, I related to her towards the end when she was so lost in life and didn't know what to do with her life after being on the same path for so long.

જ⁀➴ Luther: New book boyfriend alert?? I absolutely adored him; I wish we got more of him in this book, because I enjoyed every scene he was in. His scenes were enough to make me swoon, and I needed more. He’s a very broody MMC because of his upbringing and the role he has to serve, but he can be so gentle to the ones he loves and respects—especially his sister. Even Maura, too. I would love to talk more about him, but we haven't gotten enough of him to, so I'll bless your eyes with the two following quotes.

「✦ “You think I fear my own death?” he whispered in my ear. “Every day I draw breath is as much a curse as a gift. I’ve been living on borrowed time for longer than you can imagine. If you’re the way my fate finally catches up to me, I can’t fathom a more beautiful end.” ✦」

「✦ Without pulling away from my dagger, he turned his face, hot breath spilling over my cheek as his mouth trailed the line of my jaw. His eyes rose to mine. “Let me die with the taste of you on my lips.” ✦」

⋮ ⌗ ┆ 𝐒𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬:

જ⁀➴ Andrei Bellator and Teller: I loved her father so much at the beginning, but towards the end I was so disappointed and upset by the sudden change in his personality. He was this very decent and gentle father, and all of a sudden, he became ANGRY—that felt so forced to me. It didn’t seem like him, and I really hope this doesn’t become a common theme in the upcoming books. I get why he was upset, of course, but it still shocked me since we never saw this side of him before. Teller is adorable, and I love him so much—I’m adopting him. He’s so sweet to everyone around him. I’m attached to both characters, and that scares me. Good families never live in romantasy, but I really hope they do.

જ⁀➴ Lily: It felt like a breath of fresh air to see a sibling in the royal family that didn’t act like a spoiled brat. All because she was raised by Luther. I loved Lily and her “friendship” with Teller. I’m hoping to see more of them later on. I didn’t care at all about the mother.

જ⁀➴ Maura: I loved Maura, and I think she deserved better from Diem.

જ⁀➴ Henri: I can’t stand him. He’s such a boring character, and I hated him even more towards the end.

── .✦ 𝓕𝓲𝓷𝓪𝓵 𝓣𝓱𝓸𝓾𝓰𝓱𝓽𝓼: Overall, this was a very fun read. Predictable plot twists and cliché tension, but still enjoyable nonetheless. I can't wait to dive more into the series.

This romantasy was SO unbelievably worth the hype, and I'm annoyed at myself for letting it sit on my shelf for that long. I flew through it in one sitting, which I didn't expect to happen.

Diem has made peace with her life as a mortal healer, spending her days in a realm where immortals descended from gods rule. That is until her mother mysteriously disappears, and Diem gets the chance to join the growing rebellion, as unrest increases. And she's able to infiltrate the castle, yet the enigmatic and charming royal heir may uproot her world.

The world-building was seamless, and I was immediately able to get into the story, since it wasn't bogged down by info-dumping. I loved the creativity of the magic system, immortals, and division of the realms. And I hope we see more of the other realms in the subsequent books.

Also, the way the immortals ruled the mortals + the brewing civil war and rebellion read almost like a dystopian but in a magical setting. I seriously could not stop turning the pages, since there was continuous action and plot drivers in every scene.

I loved Diem...these healer FMCs are fantastic. She was so capable and commanding when she did her job. There were many scenes that I think healthcare workers will relate to. And I loved how she had a great relationship with her brother.

This was not romance-heavy, and I really appreciated the slow burn. I'm not a fan of characters instantaneously getting together in book one of a fantasy series, so I'm so excited to see how the enemies to lovers will progress!

2 frustrating stars, because the fmc drove me nuts.

Diem is the embodiment of all my most hated ya/na romantasy troupes. She’s reckless and doesn’t care how her actions impact others, and doesn’t learn from her actions. She thinks she’s a badass and feisty and brave, but she’s really just selfish and stupid. She makes random sexist comments to men, a troupe I hate that authors use to make their fmcs appear “tough”. Making your fmc take on the qualities of douchey 80s action hero’s doesn’t make your fmc seem tough, just sexist and dumb as hell. I get that she’s most likely a Descended from Fortos, so “fighting” is in her nature, but man it still makes her look reckless and crazy and dumb. Hurting her friends and loved ones just bc she’s about to hulk out was not a look.

Don’t even get me started on the love triangle. Think Peta and Gale from the Hunger Games, but 1000x worse.

Also in a world where people have to grow up fast, Diem acts like she’s a 12 year old girl in Sephora who’s mom won’t get her the $100 eye cream that she saw on instagram.

The ending of this book made me want to throw my phone across the room. Her quitting being a healer just bc she doesn’t want to do it anymore, even though it was one of the main sources of income for her family? And she got all pouty when her dad asked her to chip in? Like bro there’s a war on and you don’t want to do your job bc you don’t “feel like it anymore”? I wish I could do that with my job lmao and I live in the fricken suburbs.

The lack of character development for Diem drove me nuts she never learned from her mistakes and only got more selfish.

Also the LGBTQ+ rep was terrible in this book. I usually don’t like to go after authors on that, but I’m really tired of people using the community or examples of people in the community as a way of selling their books and making themselves seem inclusive. Can we get books where the random “Aunt” or side character isn’t just there to show that the main character is down with the LGBTQ+ community. Like can these characters play a role in the plot and not just be there to be the main characters set pieces or character armor.If your going to represent the community can you do it well and not make it seem like your hetero characters are there just to use them as props.

I’m going to read the next book as I hear the pacing and characters get a bit better. But it might be awhile before I try it.

3.5⭐️ I’m honestly a little conflicted over this one, but it was nonetheless a fun and fast-paced read! While it didn’t stand out to me as much as I was hoping, I’m still curious to see where the series goes.

Our FMC, Diem, can be impulsive and make rash decisions without fully considering the consequences, but I appreciated that her actions were driven by an incredibly strong sense of injustice and desire to help those around her in a greater capacity than she can as a healer. She genuinely cares about people, and I think that made it easier to understand where she was coming from even when I didn’t agree with her choices. She’s also hilarious, which made her character even more relatable and real.

So far, we don’t know too much about our MMC, Luther, but I’m anticipating a lot more character development from him over the next couple of books. I know Luther and Diem’s relationship is supposed to be a slow-burn, but I do wish they had a few more on-page interactions before their first kiss. A little more buildup and tension beforehand would have definitely made that moment feel even more satisfying and hard-won.

Overall, a promising, if slightly overhyped, first book! I’ll most likely continue the series, but I probably won’t prioritize the next book at the very top of my TBR.
